podcast.title: Daniel Greaves' Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Singer Daniel Greaves now owns and operates a bar named Motel in the Parkdale area of Toronto, which is dedicated to broadcasting Winnipeg Jets games. His commitments to the bar limit his musical activities. "Singer Daniel Grieves is far too busy running a bar called Motel in the Parkdale area of Toronto."

podcast.title: Early 1990s Prime Time Success
podcast.body: The Watchmen were listed as one of the Canadian bands achieving "prime time" exposure and success in the early 1990s. "The early 90s were pretty amazing with a long list of Canadian bands getting a shot at prime time. We had moist, the watchman, lowest of the low, sons of freedom, grapes of wrath, rhymes with orange, pure Gandarva's limb lifter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Early Success
podcast.body: The Watchmen formed in Winnipeg in 1988 and quickly achieved their first gold record in 1991, establishing their presence in the Canadian music industry. Their early career included extensive Cross Canada tours, festival appearances, and Juno nominations. "They were formed in Winnipeg in 1988, had their first gold record in 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Initial Breakup and Farewell Tour
podcast.body: By 2003, the band decided that playing "just wasn't fun anymore," leading to the announcement of a farewell tour and their subsequent breakup. This marked a temporary cessation of their active musical career. "by 2003 it just wasn't fun anymore, so they announced a farewell tour and broke up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Joey Serlin's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Guitarist Joey Serlin transitioned into a career as a composer for video games and films, establishing his own company, Vapor RMW. This career shift allowed him to continue working in music in a different capacity. "Gataris Joey Surlin works as a composer for things like video games and films. His company is called Vapor RMW."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Ken Tizzard's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Bass player Ken Tizzard worked with Ian Thornley's band for a period before embarking on a solo career, releasing two solo albums, one of which came out in 2018. This demonstrates his continued dedication to music as an independent artist. "Baseplayer Ken Tizzard worked with Ian Thornley's band for a while before releasing a couple of Sola Welvens, one came out in 2018."

podcast.title: Management Trust Client
podcast.body: The Watchmen were managed by The Management Trust, the same company that managed The Tragically Hip and Big Wreck. "And the watchman at that time."

podcast.title: Opening Act
podcast.body: Big Wreck opened a few shows for The Watchmen during a summer in Canada. "we opened a few shows for the headstone and a few shows for the watchman."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reunion and Occasional Gigs
podcast.body: The band's breakup proved temporary, as they reunited in 2008 for "occasional gigs." This non-serious reunion allowed them to continue performing sporadically. "in 2008, there was a reunion. Nothing too serious, just the occasional gig."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Sammy Kohn's Post-Band Career
podcast.body: Drummer Sammy Kohn pursued a career outside of music, initially selling advertisements for Toronto Life Magazine, then working as an account director at Spotify Canada, and is now active in real estate. His professional path diversified considerably after his time with the band. "drummer Sammy Cohn was that he sold ads for Toronto Life Magazine, and then worked for a while as an account director at Spotify Canada. And now he's back selling real estate."

xref.body: Big Wreck was managed by The Management Trust, a Canadian management company known for also representing The Tragically Hip, The Watchmen, and Andrew Cash at the time. The Management Trust played a crucial role in securing studio time and facilitating the band's early career development. "We had, we had management. We had the management trust."
